story: In April 1644 Li Zicheng's rebel army entered Beijing. The Chongzhen Emperor hanged himself on the hill behind the palace, ending the Ming in the north. The best Ming army left was at Shanhai Pass, where the Great Wall meets the sea, under the general Wu Sangui, facing the Qing beyond the wall.

Li tried to win Wu over, but his men had seized Wu's family in Beijing; legend says they also took his favorite concubine, Chen Yuanyuan. Wu turned to the Qing regent Dorgon and opened the pass. When Li attacked in May, Wu's troops fought hard, and then the Qing banner cavalry charged through a sandstorm and routed the rebels. Li fled west. In early June the Qing entered Beijing and made it their capital.
story_zh: 1644年4月，李自成的起义军攻入北京，崇祯帝在宫后的煤山自缢，明朝在北方灭亡。当时明朝剩下的最精锐的部队，是吴三桂率领的驻守山海关的大军，他们正面对关外的清军。
李自成想招降吴三桂，但他的部下在北京扣押了吴的家人，传说还抢走了吴的爱妾陈圆圆。吴三桂转而向清朝摄政王多尔衮求援，打开了山海关。5月李自成率军来攻，吴军奋力死战，清军八旗骑兵趁着风沙冲入战场，大败起义军。李自成向西逃去。6月初，清军进入北京，并定都于此。
shanhai.why: The battle let the Qing, a state of only a few hundred thousand Manchus, take over the Ming capital and begin the conquest of all China.
shanhai.why_zh: 这一战使只有几十万人口的满洲政权得以占领明朝都城，开始了征服全中国的进程。

quote.zh: 恸哭六军俱缟素，冲冠一怒为红颜。
quote.en: The whole army wept and dressed in mourning white; his fury, hair raised against his cap, was for a beauty's sake.
quote.from: Wu Weiye, Song of Yuanyuan 吴伟业《圆圆曲》

story: After taking Beijing, the Qing sent Prince Dodo south against the Southern Ming court in Nanjing. The court was divided by quarrels, and its generals were unreliable. The minister Shi Kefa took charge of the defense of Yangzhou, the key city north of the Yangtze, with too few troops.

Dodo's army reached Yangzhou in May 1645 and bombarded the walls with cannon. Shi Kefa refused repeated offers to surrender. On 20 May the city fell, and Shi was captured and killed. For about ten days Qing soldiers killed, raped and looted. A survivor, Wang Xiuchu, wrote an eyewitness account, Ten Days in Yangzhou, which put the dead at 800,000, surely an exaggeration. Nanjing surrendered a few weeks later.
story_zh: 攻占北京后，清朝派豫亲王多铎南下进攻南京的南明朝廷。南明朝中党争激烈，将领各怀异心。兵部尚书史可法负责坚守长江以北的重镇扬州，但兵力严重不足。
1645年5月，多铎大军抵达扬州，用大炮轰击城墙。史可法多次拒绝劝降。5月20日城破，史可法被俘遇害。此后约十天，清军在城中烧杀抢掠。幸存者王秀楚写下亲历记录《扬州十日记》，称死者达八十万，这个数字肯定有所夸大。几周后南京投降。
yangzhou-massacre.why: The massacre broke the will of many southern cities to resist, and Shi Kefa became a symbol of loyalty. The memory fed anti-Manchu feeling into the 1900s.
yangzhou-massacre.why_zh: 扬州屠城使江南许多城市丧失了抵抗意志，史可法则成为忠贞的象征。直到20世纪初，这段记忆仍在激发反满情绪。

people.name: Wang Xiuchu
people.role_zh: 幸存者、《扬州十日记》作者

story: Manchu men shaved the front of their heads and wore the rest of their hair in a long braid, the queue. Han Chinese men traditionally let their hair grow and tied it in a topknot, believing the body and hair were a gift from their parents that should not be harmed.

In July 1645, after Nanjing fell, the regent Dorgon ordered every Han man to adopt the Manchu hairstyle within ten days, on pain of death. People summed it up as 'keep your hair and lose your head, or keep your head and lose your hair'. The order set off fierce resistance in the Yangtze delta. Jiangyin held out for 81 days, and Jiading was sacked three times. Clothing styles were also changed to Manchu ones for men.
story_zh: 满洲男子剃去前额的头发，把其余头发编成一条长辫。汉族男子则传统上蓄发结髻，认为"身体发肤，受之父母，不敢毁伤"。
1645年7月，南京陷落后，摄政王多尔衮下令汉族男子十日之内一律改从满洲发式，违者处死。民间流传说"留头不留发，留发不留头"。剃发令在江南激起了激烈反抗：江阴军民守城八十一天，嘉定城三次遭到屠戮。男子服饰也被要求改从满洲样式。
queue-order.why: The queue became the visible sign of loyalty to the Qing. Cutting it off became a sign of revolution in the early 1900s.
queue-order.why_zh: 辫子成了效忠清朝的外在标志。到20世纪初，剪辫子则成了参加革命的象征。

people.name: Yan Yingyuan
people.role: Leader of the defense of Jiangyin

story: Zheng Chenggong, known in the West as Koxinga, was the son of a Chinese pirate-merchant and a Japanese mother. When his father surrendered to the Qing, he refused and led a powerful fleet in the cause of the Southern Ming. In 1659 he sailed up the Yangtze and besieged Nanjing, but was badly defeated.

Needing a safe base, he turned to Taiwan, where the Dutch East India Company had a colony centered on Fort Zeelandia. In April 1661 he landed with about 25,000 men. The Dutch held the fort for nine months, but in February 1662 Governor Frederick Coyett surrendered and the Dutch left the island. Koxinga died a few months later, and his son Zheng Jing ruled Taiwan.
story_zh: 郑成功是一位海商兼海盗首领的儿子，母亲是日本人，西方称他为"国姓爷"。他的父亲郑芝龙降清，郑成功却拒绝投降，率领强大的水师拥护南明。1659年他率军溯长江而上围攻南京，结果大败。
为了寻找安全的根据地，他把目光投向台湾。当时荷兰东印度公司以热兰遮城为中心统治着台湾部分地区。1661年4月，郑成功率约两万五千人登陆。荷兰人坚守了九个月，1662年2月，荷兰长官揆一投降，荷兰人撤离台湾。几个月后郑成功病逝，由儿子郑经继续统治台湾。
koxinga.why: Koxinga ended Dutch rule and began large-scale Han Chinese settlement and government of Taiwan. He is honored as a hero in both mainland China and Taiwan.
koxinga.why_zh: 郑成功结束了荷兰人的殖民统治，开启了汉人对台湾的大规模开发与治理。海峡两岸都尊他为民族英雄。

story: The Kangxi Emperor came to the throne in 1661 at the age of seven. His father's will named four Manchu regents to govern for him. One of them, the veteran general Oboi, gradually dominated the others. In 1667 he had his rival Suksaha and his family executed against the young emperor's wishes.

Kangxi, by then formally ruling, saw that he had to act. He gathered a group of young Manchu guards who practiced wrestling with him in the palace. In 1669, when Oboi came to an audience, the youths seized him. Kangxi then announced Oboi's crimes. Out of respect for his past service Oboi was spared execution and imprisoned, and he died in prison. His supporters were removed from office.
story_zh: 康熙帝1661年即位时只有七岁。父亲顺治帝遗诏任命四位满洲大臣辅政，其中老将鳌拜逐渐压倒了其他人。1667年，他不顾少年皇帝的意愿，把政敌苏克萨哈全家处死。
此时已经亲政的康熙帝意识到必须动手。他挑选了一批年轻的满洲侍卫，在宫中陪他练习摔跤。1669年，鳌拜入宫觐见时，这些少年一拥而上将他擒住。康熙帝随即宣布鳌拜的罪状，念他过去有功，免于死罪，改为囚禁，鳌拜后来死在狱中。他的党羽也都被罢免。
oboi.why: At fifteen Kangxi became master of his own government and went on to rule for 61 years, the longest reign in Chinese history.
oboi.why_zh: 十五岁的康熙帝从此真正掌握朝政，此后在位六十一年，是中国历史上在位时间最长的皇帝。

people.name: Suksaha
people.role_zh: 被鳌拜杀害的辅政大臣

story: To conquer the south, the Qing relied on Chinese generals who had changed sides. Three of them were rewarded with huge fiefs: Wu Sangui in Yunnan and Guizhou, Shang Kexi in Guangdong and Geng Jingzhong in Fujian. They ran their own armies and taxes and cost the court a fortune.

In 1673 Shang Kexi asked to retire. The young Kangxi Emperor used the chance to abolish all three fiefs. Wu Sangui rebelled at the end of the year, and the other two soon joined. The rebels took most of the south, and Wu proclaimed his own dynasty, Zhou. But Kangxi held firm, relying more and more on Han Chinese troops of the Green Standard Army. Wu died in 1678, and in 1681 Kunming fell.
story_zh: 为了征服南方，清朝依靠了一批投降的汉人将领，其中三人得到了巨大的封地：吴三桂镇守云南、贵州，尚可喜镇守广东，耿精忠镇守福建。他们拥兵自重，自行征税，朝廷还要为他们支付巨额开支。
1673年，尚可喜请求告老还乡。年轻的康熙帝趁机决定撤销三藩。当年年底吴三桂起兵反清，另外两藩不久也相继响应。叛军一度占领南方大部分地区，吴三桂还建立了自己的"周"朝。但康熙帝毫不动摇，越来越多地起用汉人组成的绿营兵。1678年吴三桂病死，1681年昆明被攻破。
three-feudatories.why: Victory made Kangxi the real master of China and removed the last great military rivals to Qing rule on the mainland.
three-feudatories.why_zh: 平定三藩使康熙帝真正掌控了全国，清朝在大陆上再也没有强大的军事对手。

story: After Koxinga's death, his son Zheng Jing and then his young grandson Zheng Keshuang ruled Taiwan as the Kingdom of Tungning. Once the Three Feudatories were defeated, the Kangxi Emperor turned to the island. He chose Shi Lang, a former officer of Koxinga who had joined the Qing after Koxinga killed his family, to lead the navy.

In July 1683 Shi Lang's fleet of about 300 ships attacked the Zheng navy at the Penghu islands. After several days of fighting, the Zheng commander Liu Guoxuan fled with only a few ships. Zheng Keshuang surrendered without further battle. Some at court wanted to abandon Taiwan, but Shi Lang argued that it protected the coast. In 1684 the island became a prefecture of Fujian province.
story_zh: 郑成功死后，他的儿子郑经、孙子郑克塽先后统治台湾，政权称为东宁。平定三藩后，康熙帝把目光转向台湾。他任命施琅为水师提督。施琅原是郑成功的部将，因家人被郑成功所杀而投降清朝。
1683年7月，施琅率领约三百艘战船在澎湖进攻郑氏水师，经过数日激战，郑军主将刘国轩只带着少数船只逃走。郑克塽随即不战而降。朝中有人主张放弃台湾，施琅力陈台湾是东南沿海的屏障。1684年，清朝设立台湾府，隶属福建省。
taiwan-1683.why: This was the first time Taiwan came under the direct rule of a government based on the mainland. It remained part of the Qing until 1895.
taiwan-1683.why_zh: 这是台湾第一次由大陆政权直接管辖，此后一直属于清朝，直到1895年。

story: In the 1650s Russian Cossacks built a fort at Albazin on the upper Amur River and used it as a base to collect furs and grain from local peoples. The Qing, busy with the Three Feudatories, could not respond at first. In the 1680s Kangxi built up forces and supply bases in the northeast.

In June 1685 a Qing army under Pengchun and Langtan besieged Albazin with cannon. The small Russian garrison surrendered and was allowed to leave. But the Russians soon came back and rebuilt the fort stronger. In 1686 the Qing besieged it again. The siege lasted months, and most of the defenders died of disease and hunger. It was lifted when news came that Russian envoys were on the way to negotiate.
story_zh: 17世纪50年代，俄国哥萨克在黑龙江上游修建雅克萨城，作为向当地各族征收毛皮和粮食的据点。当时清朝忙于平定三藩，无暇北顾。到17世纪80年代，康熙帝开始在东北集结兵力、建立补给基地。
1685年6月，彭春、郎坦率清军携大炮围攻雅克萨，城中的少量俄军投降，获准撤离。但俄军不久又卷土重来，把城堡修得更加坚固。1686年清军再次围城，一围数月，守军大多死于疾病和饥饿。直到传来俄国使臣即将前来谈判的消息，清军才撤围。
albazin.why: The sieges forced Russia to negotiate and led directly to the Treaty of Nerchinsk in 1689.
albazin.why_zh: 雅克萨之战迫使俄国坐上谈判桌，直接促成了1689年的《尼布楚条约》。

story: In the mid-1600s Russian Cossacks and traders pushed east across Siberia to the Amur River, building forts such as Albazin and collecting fur tribute from local peoples. The Qing saw the Amur region as its homeland's back door. After Qing troops besieged Albazin in 1685 and 1686, both sides agreed to talk.

In 1689 the Qing envoys Songgotu and Tong Guogang met the Russian envoy Fyodor Golovin at Nerchinsk. Two Jesuits, Jean-François Gerbillon and Thomas Pereira, translated, and the official text was in Latin. The treaty set the border along the Argun River and the Stanovoy mountains, giving the Amur basin to the Qing. Russia destroyed Albazin, and the two empires allowed trade with passports.
story_zh: 17世纪中叶，俄国哥萨克和商人越过西伯利亚向东推进到黑龙江流域，修筑雅克萨等据点，向当地各族征收毛皮。清朝把黑龙江一带视为龙兴之地的后方。1685年和1686年清军两次围攻雅克萨后，双方同意谈判。
1689年，清朝使臣索额图、佟国纲与俄国使臣戈洛文在尼布楚会谈。耶稣会士张诚和徐日升担任翻译，正式文本用拉丁文写成。条约规定以额尔古纳河和外兴安岭为界，黑龙江流域归属清朝。俄国拆毁雅克萨城，两国人民持护照可以往来贸易。
nerchinsk.why: Nerchinsk kept peace between the two empires for over 150 years, until Russia took the Amur lands in 1858 and 1860.
nerchinsk.why_zh: 《尼布楚条约》使中俄两国和平相处了一百五十多年，直到1858年和1860年沙俄割占黑龙江以北和乌苏里江以东的土地。

story: Galdan, ruler of the Dzungars in the west, invaded the lands of the Khalkha Mongols in 1688, and many Khalkha fled south and submitted to the Qing. In 1690 Galdan pushed within a few hundred kilometers of Beijing before a Qing army checked him at Ulan Butung.

In 1696 the Kangxi Emperor led a great campaign across the Gobi in person, in three columns. As the emperor's column approached from the east, Galdan retreated west into the path of the western column under Fiyanggū. At Jao Modo, near the Tuul River, Fiyanggū's troops held a hill and then attacked. Galdan's army was destroyed, and his wife Anu was killed. Galdan fled with a few followers and died the next year.
story_zh: 西部的准噶尔首领噶尔丹于1688年进攻喀尔喀蒙古，许多喀尔喀部众南逃归附清朝。1690年，噶尔丹一度推进到离北京只有几百公里的地方，在乌兰布通被清军挡住。
1696年，康熙帝亲率大军分三路穿越戈壁北征。皇帝亲率的中路军从东面逼近，噶尔丹向西撤退，正好撞上费扬古率领的西路军。在土拉河附近的昭莫多，费扬古的军队抢占山头，随后发起进攻。噶尔丹大败，妻子阿奴战死。噶尔丹只带着少数随从逃走，次年死去。
jao-modo.why: The victory brought Outer Mongolia firmly under Qing rule and began the long Qing–Dzungar struggle that ended in 1757.
jao-modo.why_zh: 这场胜利使外蒙古牢固地归入清朝统治，也开启了此后一直延续到1757年的清准战争。

story: The Kangxi Emperor was a keen scholar who sponsored many large books. In 1710 he ordered the grand secretaries Zhang Yushu and Chen Tingjing to lead a team of about thirty scholars in making a complete dictionary of Chinese characters, improving on earlier Ming dictionaries.

The dictionary was finished in 1716. It contains about 47,000 characters arranged under 214 radicals and then by the number of strokes. For each character it gives pronunciations, meanings and quotations from earlier texts showing how it was used. It includes many rare and variant forms. It was the largest Chinese dictionary of its time. Scholars have since found many errors in it, but it set the standard for organizing characters.
story_zh: 康熙帝喜好学问，主持编纂了许多大型典籍。1710年，他命大学士张玉书、陈廷敬带领约三十名学者，在明代字书的基础上编一部完备的汉字字典。
字典于1716年完成，收字约四万七千个，先按214个部首、再按笔画数排列。每个字都注明读音、字义，并引用古书中的用例，还收录了许多生僻字和异体字。它是当时规模最大的汉语字典。后人发现书中有不少错误，但它确立了汉字编排的标准。
kangxi-dictionary.why: Its 214 radicals are still the standard way to look up characters in traditional dictionaries and are used in the Unicode computer standard.
kangxi-dictionary.why_zh: 它的214部首至今仍是传统字典的查字标准，也被计算机编码标准Unicode采用。

story: In 1717 a Dzungar army from the west crossed the high desert, took Lhasa and killed Lha-bzang Khan, the Khoshut Mongol ruler of Tibet. The Dzungars looted the city and attacked the monasteries of other schools. A first Qing relief force was wiped out in 1718.

In 1720 the Kangxi Emperor sent two larger armies, one from Qinghai and one from Sichuan. They escorted a young lama, Kelzang Gyatso, whom many Tibetans and Mongols already recognized as the Seventh Dalai Lama. The Dzungars withdrew, and in the autumn the boy was enthroned in the Potala Palace. The Qing left a garrison and set up a Tibetan council. After civil war in Tibet in 1727, it stationed two resident officials, the ambans, in Lhasa.
story_zh: 1717年，准噶尔军从西面穿越高原荒漠，攻占拉萨，杀死统治西藏的和硕特蒙古首领拉藏汗。准噶尔军在拉萨大肆劫掠，还攻击其他教派的寺院。1718年清朝派出的第一支援军全军覆没。
1720年，康熙帝派出两路大军，一路从青海、一路从四川进藏，护送年轻的格桑嘉措入藏，许多藏人和蒙古人早已认定他是七世达赖喇嘛。准噶尔军撤走，当年秋天格桑嘉措在布达拉宫坐床。清朝在西藏留驻军队，设立噶伦共同理政。1727年西藏发生内乱后，清朝开始向拉萨派驻两名驻藏大臣。
qing-tibet.why: The expedition began two centuries of Qing authority in Tibet, which became the basis of later Chinese claims and remains contested.
qing-tibet.why_zh: 这次出兵开启了清朝在西藏长达两个世纪的统治，成为后来中国对西藏主权主张的依据，这一问题至今仍有争议。

story: Under the old system, adult men paid a poll tax called ding in addition to the land tax. Poor men with no land still had to pay, so many hid from the census or fled. In 1712 the Kangxi Emperor declared that the number of taxable men would be frozen at the 1711 level, and that new adults would 'never have their tax raised'.

His son, the Yongzheng Emperor, went further. From 1723, province by province, the fixed poll tax quota was added to the land tax and collected according to the amount of land a family owned. A man with no land now paid no poll tax. Yongzheng also stopped officials from keeping extra fees for themselves, turning them into regular payments to support honest administration.
story_zh: 按照旧制，成年男子除了缴纳田赋，还要缴纳按人头计算的丁银。没有土地的穷人也得交，许多人只好隐瞒户口或逃亡。1712年，康熙帝宣布以1711年的人丁数为定额，以后新增人口"永不加赋"。
他的儿子雍正帝更进一步。从1723年起，各省陆续把固定的丁银摊入田赋，按照各家田地多少征收，没有土地的人从此不再交人头税。雍正帝还实行"耗羡归公"，禁止官员私收附加费，把它变成正式收入，用来发放养廉银。
tanding-rumu.why: The reform eased the burden on the poor, ended the incentive to hide from the census, and helped the recorded population soar past 300 million by 1800.
tanding-rumu.why_zh: 这项改革减轻了穷人的负担，人们不再需要隐匿户口，到1800年登记人口迅速增长到三亿以上。

people.name: Kangxi Emperor
people.role: Emperor who froze the head tax

story: Around 1729, while preparing for war against the Dzungars, the Yongzheng Emperor set up a small office inside the palace to handle military affairs quickly and secretly. It met in simple rooms near his living quarters, the Hall of Mental Cultivation. It soon became known as the Junjichu, the Grand Council.

The council had only a few members, chosen personally by the emperor from Manchu and Han officials, such as Zhang Tingyu. They met him daily, drafted his edicts and handled the secret memorials that officials across the empire sent straight to the emperor. Over time the council took over most important decisions, while the old Grand Secretariat handled routine paperwork.
story_zh: 大约在1729年，雍正帝为准备对准噶尔用兵，在宫中设立了一个小机构，以便迅速而秘密地处理军务。它设在皇帝起居的养心殿附近，房屋十分简朴，不久便被称为军机处。
军机处人数很少，由皇帝从满汉官员中亲自挑选，比如张廷玉。军机大臣每天面见皇帝，起草谕旨，处理各地官员直接呈送皇帝的密折。后来军机处逐渐掌握了几乎所有重大决策，原来的内阁只处理日常公文。
grand-council.why: The Grand Council gave Qing emperors close personal control over government and remained the heart of the state until 1911.
grand-council.why_zh: 军机处使清朝皇帝能够直接、牢固地掌控朝政，直到1911年一直是国家的权力中枢。

story: The Dzungars were the last great nomadic empire of the steppe, based in the Ili valley. For seventy years they fought the Qing over Mongolia and Tibet. After their ruler Galdan Tseren died in 1745, his heirs fought each other, and in 1754 the prince Amursana fled to the Qing and asked for help.

In 1755 Qing armies, guided by Amursana, took Ili almost without a fight. Amursana then rebelled, hoping to become khan himself. Qianlong ordered that the Dzungars be wiped out. Between Qing campaigns, massacres and a smallpox epidemic, most of the Dzungar people died by 1758. Amursana fled to Russia and died of smallpox. In 1759 Qing forces also conquered the oasis cities of the Tarim Basin.
story_zh: 准噶尔是草原上最后一个强大的游牧帝国，以伊犁河谷为中心，与清朝争夺蒙古和西藏长达七十年。1745年首领噶尔丹策零死后，继承人互相残杀，1754年贵族阿睦尔撒纳投奔清朝求援。
1755年，清军在阿睦尔撒纳引导下几乎兵不血刃地攻占伊犁。随后阿睦尔撒纳想自立为汗，起兵反清。乾隆帝下令剿灭准噶尔。在清军征讨、屠杀和天花流行的共同打击下，到1758年大部分准噶尔人已经死亡。阿睦尔撒纳逃往俄国，死于天花。1759年清军又平定了塔里木盆地的绿洲城市。
dzungar.why: The conquest doubled the Qing's territory in the northwest and created the region named Xinjiang, the 'new frontier'. It also destroyed the Dzungar people.
dzungar.why_zh: 这场征服使清朝西北的疆域扩大了一倍，形成了被称为"新疆"的地区，准噶尔人也几乎被灭绝。

story: In the 1750s the British East India Company tried to trade at Ningbo and other ports to get closer to the tea and silk regions and avoid the high fees at Guangzhou. In 1757 the Qianlong Emperor ordered that Western ships could trade only at Guangzhou. The British trader James Flint, who protested to Beijing, was jailed for three years.

At Guangzhou, foreign merchants had to deal through a small group of licensed Chinese firms, the Cohong. They lived in a row of warehouses, the Thirteen Factories, outside the city walls, could stay only during the trading season, and were forbidden to bring in their wives or learn Chinese from local teachers. All contact with officials went through the Cohong.
story_zh: 18世纪50年代，英国东印度公司试图到宁波等港口贸易，以便靠近茶叶和丝绸产地，并避开广州的高额规费。1757年，乾隆帝下令西洋商船只准在广州一口通商。英国商人洪任辉进京告状，结果被关押了三年。
在广州，外国商人只能通过少数特许的中国行商（公行）做生意。他们住在城外的一排商馆，即十三行里，只能在贸易季节停留，不许带妻子来，也不许向当地人学习汉语。与官府的一切往来都要通过行商转达。
canton-system.why: The system kept foreign trade under tight control for 85 years, but British frustration with it helped lead to the Opium War, which ended it in 1842.
canton-system.why_zh: 这一制度把对外贸易严格控制了八十五年，但英国人对它的不满也是鸦片战争的原因之一，1842年它随之终结。

story: In 1773 the Qianlong Emperor ordered a collection of the most important books in Chinese, divided into the four traditional branches: classics, history, philosophy and literature. The scholar Ji Yun led a team of hundreds of editors and thousands of copyists.

About 3,500 works were copied by hand into some 36,000 volumes. The first set was finished in 1782, and seven sets were made and kept in libraries in Beijing, Shenyang, Chengde, Yangzhou, Zhenjiang and Hangzhou. The project also had a darker side, for it doubled as a search of private libraries across the empire. Books seen as anti-Manchu or disrespectful were searched out, and about 3,000 titles were banned and destroyed, while others were altered.
story_zh: 1773年，乾隆帝下令把中国最重要的典籍汇编成一部大丛书，按照传统分为经、史、子、集四部。学者纪昀主持其事，参与编校的有数百人，抄写人员达数千人。
约三千五百种书籍被手抄成约三万六千册。第一部于1782年完成，前后共抄七部，分藏在北京、沈阳、承德、扬州、镇江和杭州的藏书阁中。这项工程也有阴暗的一面，它同时也是对全国私人藏书的一次大搜查：凡被认为有反满或不敬内容的书籍都被搜查出来，约三千种遭到禁毁，还有不少书被删改。
siku-quanshu.why: The Siku Quanshu is the largest collection of books in Chinese history and preserved many works, but it was also one of the largest acts of censorship.
siku-quanshu.why_zh: 《四库全书》是中国历史上规模最大的丛书，保存了大量典籍，但同时也是一次规模空前的文化审查。

story: Cao Xueqin grew up in a rich family that ran the imperial silk works in Nanjing, but in 1728 the family's property was seized and they moved to Beijing in reduced circumstances. In poverty in the hills west of Beijing he spent years writing a long novel, The Story of the Stone. When he died around 1763, about 80 chapters were circulating in hand-copied manuscripts.

In 1791 Cheng Weiyuan and Gao E printed a 120-chapter version with movable type, adding 40 chapters that completed the story. The novel follows the great Jia family, the sensitive young Jia Baoyu, his cousin Lin Daiyu whom he loves, and Xue Baochai whom he is made to marry. It portrays hundreds of characters and the slow decline of the family.
story_zh: 曹雪芹出身于世代掌管江宁织造的富贵之家，1728年曹家被抄，迁回北京，家道中落。他晚年在北京西山过着贫困的生活，花了多年时间写一部长篇小说《石头记》。约1763年他去世时，大约八十回的手抄本已在流传。
1791年，程伟元、高鹗用活字印出一百二十回本，补上了后四十回，使故事完整。小说讲述贾府这个大家族的故事：多情敏感的贾宝玉，他深爱的表妹林黛玉，以及他被安排迎娶的薛宝钗。书中刻画了几百个人物，写尽一个家族的由盛转衰。
red-chamber.why: Dream of the Red Chamber is generally considered the greatest Chinese novel. Its study, called 'Redology', is a field of scholarship of its own.
red-chamber.why_zh: 《红楼梦》被公认为中国最伟大的小说，专门研究它的学问被称为"红学"。

people.name: Gao E
people.role_zh: 一百二十回本的整理者

quote.zh: 满纸荒唐言，一把辛酸泪。都云作者痴，谁解其中味？
quote.en: Pages full of absurd words, a handful of bitter tears. All call the author a fool; who understands the taste within?
quote.from: Dream of the Red Chamber, chapter 1 《红楼梦》第一回

story: By the 1790s Britain bought huge amounts of tea from China but could trade only at Guangzhou under strict rules. King George III sent Lord George Macartney with a large embassy and gifts, including scientific instruments, to ask for better terms.

Macartney met the 82-year-old Qianlong Emperor at the summer retreat in Chengde in September 1793, after a long dispute over the kowtow; in the end he knelt on one knee as he would to his own king. He asked for a permanent embassy in Beijing, more open ports, a small island for British traders and fixed tariffs. Qianlong rejected every request in a letter to George III, saying China had no need of British goods.
story_zh: 到18世纪90年代，英国从中国大量购买茶叶，但只能在广州按照严格的规定进行贸易。英王乔治三世派马戛尔尼勋爵率领庞大的使团来华，带来了科学仪器等礼物，希望改善通商条件。
1793年9月，经过一番关于叩头礼的争执，马戛尔尼在承德避暑山庄觐见了八十二岁的乾隆帝，最后按照觐见英王的礼节单膝下跪。他提出在北京常驻使节、增开通商口岸、拨给英商一个小岛以及固定关税等要求。乾隆帝在给英王的敕谕中一一拒绝，称中国并不需要英国的货物。
macartney.why: The failed embassy is often seen as a missed chance for China to engage with the West on its own terms, half a century before the Opium War.
macartney.why_zh: 这次出使的失败常被看作中国错失了一次主动与西方打交道的机会，半个世纪后便爆发了鸦片战争。

quote.zh: 天朝物产丰盈，无所不有，原不藉外夷货物以通有无。
quote.en: Our Celestial Empire possesses all things in abundance and lacks nothing; we have no need to trade for the goods of outside barbarians.
quote.from: Qianlong's edict to George III, 1793 乾隆《敕谕英吉利国王》

story: By the late 1700s millions of poor settlers had moved into the remote mountains where Hubei, Sichuan and Shaanxi meet. Life there was hard, local officials were corrupt, and many joined the White Lotus sect, which taught that the Buddha Maitreya would come to save believers from disaster.

In 1796, the year Qianlong handed the throne to his son Jiaqing, sect members rose in Hubei. Among the leaders was a young widow, Wang Cong'er. The rebels fought as mobile bands in the mountains, and the Qing armies, led by officers who were often corrupt, failed to crush them. Only after Qianlong's death in 1799, when Jiaqing removed the corrupt minister Heshen, did a new strategy of fortified villages and local militias defeat them by 1804.
story_zh: 到18世纪末，数以百万计的贫苦移民涌入湖北、四川、陕西交界的深山老林。那里生活艰难，地方官吏贪腐，许多人加入了白莲教。白莲教宣扬弥勒佛将降世，救信徒脱离劫难。
1796年，也就是乾隆帝把皇位传给儿子嘉庆帝的那一年，白莲教徒在湖北起事，首领中有一位年轻的寡妇王聪儿。起义军在山区流动作战，清军将领大多腐败无能，久剿不灭。直到1799年乾隆帝去世，嘉庆帝除掉贪官和珅，改用坚壁清野、修筑寨堡、招募乡勇的办法，才在1804年把起义镇压下去。
white-lotus.why: The war cost about 200 million taels and exposed the decay of the banner armies. It marks the start of the Qing's decline.
white-lotus.why_zh: 这场战争耗费军费约两亿两白银，暴露了八旗、绿营的腐朽，被视为清朝由盛转衰的开端。

story: The Eight Trigrams were a group of White Lotus-related sects in north China. In 1813 their leaders, Lin Qing near Beijing and Li Wencheng in Henan, planned a rising. Lin recruited several palace eunuchs, who promised to open the gates of the Forbidden City while the Jiaqing Emperor was away hunting in Rehe.

On 15 October 1813 about a hundred rebels, disguised as traders, entered the palace through the east and west gates with the eunuchs' help. Guards shut the east gate, but those who got in through the west fought toward the inner palace. Prince Mianning, the emperor's second son, shot two of them with a musket. Troops then arrived and killed or captured the rest. Lin Qing was arrested and executed.
story_zh: 八卦教是华北一些与白莲教有渊源的教派，又称天理教。1813年，北京附近的林清和河南的李文成计划起事。林清收买了几名宫中太监，约定趁嘉庆帝去热河围猎时打开紫禁城宫门。
1813年10月15日，约一百名教徒扮成商贩，在太监的接应下分别从东华门和西华门冲进皇宫。东华门很快被守卫关上，从西华门进入的人一路向内廷打去。皇次子旻宁用鸟枪打死了两人。随后援兵赶到，把余众全部杀死或擒获。林清被捕处死。
eight-trigrams.why: Rebels inside the Forbidden City shocked the court. Jiaqing called it something unknown in Han, Tang, Song or Ming. Mianning later became the Daoguang Emperor.
eight-trigrams.why_zh: 起义者打进紫禁城令朝廷大为震惊，嘉庆帝称这是"汉唐宋明未有之事"。旻宁后来即位为道光帝。

story: To pay for tea, British merchants smuggled ever larger amounts of Indian opium into China. By the 1830s millions of Chinese were addicted, and silver was flowing out of the country. The Daoguang Emperor sent Lin Zexu, a strict and honest official, to Guangzhou in 1839 as imperial commissioner to stop the trade.

Lin blockaded the foreign merchants in their warehouses until the British superintendent of trade, Charles Elliot, handed over about 20,000 chests of opium. From 3 June 1839, workers at Humen mixed the opium with salt and lime in large pits and flushed it into the sea; it took about three weeks. Britain treated the seizure of its merchants' property as a cause for war and sent a fleet in 1840.
story_zh: 英国商人为了支付购买茶叶的货款，把越来越多的印度鸦片走私到中国。到19世纪30年代，吸食鸦片的中国人已达数百万，白银大量外流。1839年，道光帝派为官清廉严正的林则徐以钦差大臣身份前往广州禁烟。
林则徐封锁外国商馆，迫使英国驻华商务总监义律交出约两万箱鸦片。从1839年6月3日起，工人们在虎门海滩挖池，把鸦片与盐、石灰混合销毁，再冲入大海，前后用了约三周时间。英国把收缴英商财产视为开战理由，1840年派舰队来华。
humen.why: The destruction of opium triggered the First Opium War, the start of China's 'century of humiliation'. 3 June is now an anti-drug day in China.
humen.why_zh: 虎门销烟引发了第一次鸦片战争，中国近代屈辱的百年由此开始。今天6月3日是中国的禁烟节。

story: In the First Opium War, British steamships and modern guns overwhelmed Qing coastal defenses. In 1842 a British fleet sailed up the Yangtze, took Zhenjiang and cut the Grand Canal, then appeared outside Nanjing, the old southern capital. The Qing court, fearing the loss of the canal and the south, asked for peace.

On 29 August 1842, on board the warship HMS Cornwallis, the Qing envoys Qiying and Yilibu signed a treaty with Sir Henry Pottinger. China ceded Hong Kong Island to Britain, opened five ports to trade and British residence — Guangzhou, Xiamen, Fuzhou, Ningbo and Shanghai — paid 21 million silver dollars, abolished the Cohong merchant monopoly and accepted fixed tariffs. A supplementary treaty in 1843 added extraterritoriality and most-favored-nation treatment.
story_zh: 第一次鸦片战争中，英国的蒸汽船和新式火炮压倒了清朝的沿海防御。1842年，英国舰队驶入长江，攻陷镇江，切断大运河，兵临南京城下。清廷担心运河和江南不保，只得求和。
1842年8月29日，清朝钦差大臣耆英、伊里布在英舰"皋华丽"号上与璞鼎查签订条约。中国把香港岛割让给英国，开放广州、厦门、福州、宁波、上海五处通商，允许英国人居住，赔款二千一百万银元，废除公行垄断，并实行协定关税。1843年的补充条约又加上了领事裁判权和片面最惠国待遇。
nanking.why: The treaty set the pattern of the 'unequal treaties' that limited Chinese sovereignty for a century. Hong Kong returned to China only in 1997.
nanking.why_zh: 这个条约开了"不平等条约"的先例，此后一百年间中国主权受到严重损害。香港直到1997年才回归中国。

story: Hong Xiuquan, a village teacher in Guangdong, failed the civil service exams four times. After reading a Christian tract he came to believe that he was the younger brother of Jesus, sent to destroy demons. In Guangxi he and his followers built the God Worshipping Society, and in January 1851 they rose at Jintian and proclaimed the Heavenly Kingdom of Great Peace.

The Taiping army marched north and in 1853 took Nanjing, which became their capital, Tianjing. They banned opium, foot-binding and gambling and promised shared land. But in 1856 their leaders killed each other. Zeng Guofan's Hunan army, later helped by Li Hongzhang and Western-officered troops, slowly pushed them back. Hong died in 1864 and Nanjing fell weeks later.
story_zh: 广东乡村塾师洪秀全四次科举落第。他读了一本基督教小册子后，认定自己是耶稣的弟弟，受上帝派遣下凡斩妖除魔。他和追随者在广西创立拜上帝会，1851年1月在金田起事，建号太平天国。
太平军一路北上，1853年攻占南京，定为都城，改名天京。他们禁止吸鸦片、缠足和赌博，宣扬平分土地。但1856年领导层发生内讧，互相残杀。曾国藩的湘军，后来又有李鸿章的淮军和洋人指挥的部队，逐步把太平军压了回去。1864年洪秀全病死，几周后天京陷落。
taiping.why: One of the deadliest wars in history, it killed perhaps 20 to 30 million people and shifted power from the Manchu court to Han Chinese provincial leaders.
taiping.why_zh: 这是历史上死亡人数最多的战争之一，估计有两三千万人丧生。它也使权力从满洲朝廷转移到汉族地方大员手中。

story: In the 1850s, while the Qing was fighting the Taipings and the British and French, Russia's governor of eastern Siberia, Nikolay Muravyov, sent soldiers and settlers down the Amur River and built posts along its north bank.

In May 1858 Muravyov met the Qing general Yishan at Aigun. With Russian gunboats nearby and Anglo-French forces attacking the Dagu forts far to the south, Yishan signed a treaty giving Russia the whole north bank of the Amur, more than 600,000 square kilometers. The land between the Ussuri River and the sea was to be held jointly. The Xianfeng Emperor at first refused to accept the treaty, but in 1860 the Convention of Peking confirmed it and gave Russia the Ussuri lands as well.
story_zh: 19世纪50年代，清朝正忙于对付太平天国和英法联军，俄国东西伯利亚总督穆拉维约夫趁机派兵和移民沿黑龙江而下，在北岸修建据点。
1858年5月，穆拉维约夫与黑龙江将军奕山在瑷珲会谈。俄国炮舰就在附近，南方的英法联军又正在攻打大沽炮台，奕山被迫签约，把黑龙江以北六十多万平方公里的土地割给俄国，乌苏里江以东至海的土地暂由两国共管。咸丰帝起初拒绝承认，但1860年的中俄《北京条约》不仅确认了此约，还把乌苏里江以东的土地也划给了俄国。
aigun.why: Aigun and the 1860 treaty cost the Qing about a million square kilometers in the northeast and gave Russia its Pacific port at Vladivostok.
aigun.why_zh: 《瑷珲条约》和1860年的《北京条约》使清朝在东北丧失了约一百万平方公里土地，俄国由此获得了太平洋港口海参崴。

people.name: Yishan
people.role_zh: 签约的清朝黑龙江将军

story: In 1856 Qing police boarded the Arrow, a Chinese ship registered in Hong Kong, and arrested its crew. Britain used the incident, and France the execution of a French missionary, as reasons for a new war, known as the Second Opium War. Anglo-French forces took Guangzhou in late 1857.

In May 1858 they sailed north and captured the Dagu forts guarding the approach to Tianjin. In June the Qing signed treaties at Tianjin with Britain, France, Russia and the United States. China agreed to accept foreign ministers in Beijing, open ten more ports, allow foreign ships on the Yangtze, let foreigners travel inland and missionaries preach freely, and pay indemnities. A tariff agreement later that year made the opium trade legal.
story_zh: 1856年，清朝水师登上在香港注册的中国船"亚罗号"，逮捕了船员。英国以此为借口，法国则以一名法国传教士被处死为由，发动了新的战争，史称第二次鸦片战争。1857年底，英法联军攻占广州。
1858年5月，联军北上攻陷扼守天津门户的大沽炮台。6月，清朝在天津分别与英、法、俄、美签订条约，同意外国公使常驻北京，增开十个通商口岸，允许外国船只在长江航行，外国人可以到内地游历，传教士可以自由传教，并支付赔款。同年签订的税则协定还使鸦片贸易合法化。
treaties-tianjin.why: When the Qing resisted carrying out the treaties in 1859, the war resumed, leading to the burning of the Summer Palace in 1860.
treaties-tianjin.why_zh: 1859年清朝试图阻止换约，战火重燃，最终导致1860年火烧圆明园。

story: The Yuanmingyuan, northwest of Beijing, was a vast garden of lakes, halls and pavilions built over 150 years by Qing emperors. It included European-style palaces designed by Jesuits and held countless treasures.

In 1860, in the Second Opium War, British and French troops advanced on Beijing. The Xianfeng Emperor fled to Chengde. The Qing had seized a British and French negotiating party, and about twenty prisoners died after harsh treatment. French and British soldiers first looted the gardens. Then, in October, the British envoy Lord Elgin ordered the palace burned as punishment. It burned for days. Prince Gong then signed the Convention of Peking, giving Kowloon to Britain and paying large indemnities.
story_zh: 圆明园位于北京西北郊，是清朝几代皇帝用一百五十年时间营建的皇家园林，湖泊、殿堂、亭台遍布，还有耶稣会士设计的西洋楼，园中珍宝不计其数。
1860年第二次鸦片战争中，英法联军进逼北京，咸丰帝逃往承德。此前清军扣押了英法谈判人员，约二十人因受虐待而死。法军和英军先在园中大肆抢掠。10月，英国全权代表额尔金下令火烧圆明园作为报复，大火烧了好几天。随后恭亲王签订《北京条约》，把九龙割给英国，并支付巨额赔款。
summer-palace.why: The ruins became a lasting symbol of China's humiliation by foreign powers. Many looted objects are still in Western museums.
summer-palace.why_zh: 圆明园的废墟成为中国遭受列强欺凌的永久象征，许多被抢走的文物至今仍在西方博物馆中。

people.name: Lord Elgin
people.role: British envoy who ordered the burning

story: Defeats by Britain and France and the struggle against the Taipings convinced some Qing officials that China needed Western weapons and technology. In 1861 Zeng Guofan set up an arsenal at Anqing, and the court created a foreign office, the Zongli Yamen, under Prince Gong.

Over the next decades, provincial leaders built the Jiangnan Arsenal in Shanghai, the Fuzhou Navy Yard, the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company, coal mines, telegraph lines and schools for languages and science. Li Hongzhang created the Beiyang Fleet. But the effort was patchy, controlled by rival officials and limited by conservative opposition. It did not change the political system, and much money was wasted or stolen.
story_zh: 在对英法战争中接连失败，又在镇压太平天国中吃尽苦头，一些清朝官员认识到中国需要西方的武器和技术。1861年，曾国藩在安庆创办内军械所，朝廷设立总理各国事务衙门，由恭亲王主持。
此后几十年间，各地大员相继创办了上海江南制造总局、福州船政局、轮船招商局，以及煤矿、电报线路和外语、科学学堂。李鸿章组建了北洋舰队。但这些事业各自为政，被不同的大员掌控，又受到保守派阻挠，没有触动政治制度，大量经费被浪费或侵吞。
self-strengthening.why: The movement built China's first modern industries, but defeat by Japan in 1895 showed that technology alone could not save the dynasty.
self-strengthening.why_zh: 洋务运动建立了中国最早的近代工业，但1895年败给日本说明，仅靠引进技术救不了清朝。

people.name: Zuo Zongtang
people.role: Founder of the Fuzhou Navy Yard

story: The Xianfeng Emperor died in August 1861 at Chengde, where he had fled from the Anglo-French army. His heir, Zaichun, was only five. His will named eight regents, led by the official Sushun, to rule for the boy.

The boy's mother, Consort Yi, and the late emperor's empress, both now empresses dowager, distrusted the regents. They allied with Prince Gong, the emperor's brother, who had stayed in Beijing to negotiate with the foreigners. When the funeral procession returned to Beijing in November, they struck. The regents were arrested; Sushun was beheaded and two princes were ordered to kill themselves. The two empresses dowager, Ci'an and Cixi, began to rule 'from behind the curtain', with Prince Gong as chief minister.
story_zh: 1861年8月，逃到承德避难的咸丰帝病逝，继位的载淳只有五岁。咸丰帝遗命肃顺等八位大臣辅政。
小皇帝的生母懿贵妃和咸丰帝的皇后，此时都已成为皇太后，她们对顾命大臣心存戒备，于是联合留在北京与外国人议和的咸丰帝之弟恭亲王。11月，皇帝灵柩运回北京时，她们发动政变，逮捕八大臣：肃顺被斩首，两位亲王被赐自尽。慈安、慈禧两宫太后开始"垂帘听政"，恭亲王出任议政王。
xinyou-coup.why: The coup began Cixi's nearly fifty years as the real ruler of China, through the reigns of her son and her nephew.
xinyou-coup.why_zh: 这次政变开启了慈禧近五十年的实际统治，历经她的儿子和侄子两朝。

story: After 1860 the Qing had to deal with foreign diplomats in Beijing but had almost no officials who knew foreign languages; it relied on foreigners' interpreters. In 1862 Prince Gong and the new foreign office, the Zongli Yamen, opened the Tongwen Guan, a school to train interpreters.

It began with English classes taught by a missionary, and soon added French, Russian and later German and Japanese. In 1867 the school proposed adding astronomy and mathematics and recruiting young degree-holders. Conservative officials, led by the grand secretary Woren, protested that Confucian scholars should not study Western arts. The plan went ahead but attracted few top students. The American W. A. P. Martin led the school for many years.
story_zh: 1860年后，清朝不得不在北京与外国使节打交道，却几乎没有懂外语的官员，只能依赖外国人的翻译。1862年，恭亲王和新设的总理衙门开办同文馆，专门培养翻译人才。
同文馆起初只开设英文课，由传教士任教，不久增设法文、俄文，后来又有德文和日文。1867年，同文馆提议增设天文、算学，招收年轻的科举出身者。以大学士倭仁为首的保守派强烈反对，认为儒生不应学习西洋技艺。计划虽然实行，却很少有优秀学生报考。美国人丁韪良长期担任总教习。
tongwen-guan.why: The Tongwen Guan was China's first modern government school. It was merged into the Imperial University of Peking, the forerunner of Peking University, in 1902.
tongwen-guan.why_zh: 京师同文馆是中国第一所近代官办学校，1902年并入京师大学堂，即北京大学的前身。

story: Yung Wing grew up near Macau, went to the United States as a boy and in 1854 became the first Chinese graduate of Yale. Back in China he persuaded Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang to send boys to America to learn science and engineering.

From 1872 to 1875, four groups of 30 boys, aged about ten to sixteen, sailed from Shanghai. They lived with families in Connecticut and Massachusetts, went to local schools, and many entered colleges such as Yale. They also played baseball and some became Christians, which alarmed conservative officials. In 1881 the court recalled them all. Among them were the railway engineer Zhan Tianyou and the future premier Tang Shaoyi.
story_zh: 容闳在澳门附近长大，少年时赴美，1854年成为第一个毕业于耶鲁大学的中国人。回国后，他说服曾国藩、李鸿章派遣幼童赴美学习科学技术。
1872年至1875年，四批共一百二十名十岁到十六岁左右的幼童从上海出发。他们寄住在康涅狄格州和马萨诸塞州的美国家庭中，进入当地学校读书，不少人后来考入耶鲁等大学。他们还打棒球，有些人信了基督教，这让保守官员十分不安。1881年，清廷将他们全部召回。其中有后来的铁路工程师詹天佑和民国总理唐绍仪。
educational-mission.why: Though cut short, the mission was China's first government program of study abroad, and its students became pioneers in railways, mining, the navy and diplomacy.
educational-mission.why_zh: 留美幼童计划虽然中途夭折，却是中国第一次官派留学，这些学生后来成为铁路、矿业、海军和外交领域的先驱。

people.name: Zhan Tianyou
people.role_zh: 留美学生，后来的铁路工程师

people.name: Tang Shaoyi
people.role_zh: 留美学生，后来的国务总理

story: From 1876 the rains failed for three years across north China: Shanxi, Henan, Shandong, Zhili and Shaanxi. Crops died, and grain prices rose many times over. Shanxi, cut off by mountains and without railways, was hit hardest.

People ate grass, bark and clay, and sold their children. Whole villages emptied as people died or fled. Estimates of the dead range from about 9 to 13 million. The Qing government sent relief grain and money and allowed the sale of offices to raise funds, but transport was slow and corruption widespread. Foreign missionaries such as Timothy Richard, and Chinese merchants in the south, organized private relief and spread news of the disaster in newspapers.
story_zh: 从1876年起，华北的山西、河南、山东、直隶、陕西连续三年大旱，庄稼枯死，粮价暴涨数倍。山西四面环山，没有铁路，受灾最重。
饥民吃草根、树皮、观音土，卖儿卖女，许多村庄的人或死或逃，十室九空。死亡人数估计在九百万到一千三百万之间。清廷调拨赈粮赈款，还以捐纳官职筹款，但运输迟缓，贪污严重。李提摩太等外国传教士和江南的中国商人组织了民间赈灾，并通过报纸报道灾情。
great-famine.why: The famine was one of the worst in history. It showed the state's weakness and helped spur interest in railways and modern relief work.
great-famine.why_zh: 这是历史上最惨烈的饥荒之一，暴露了国家的虚弱，也促使人们重视修建铁路和近代赈灾事业。

story: In the early 1880s France expanded its control over Vietnam, a Qing tributary state, and fighting broke out between French and Chinese forces in northern Vietnam. In July 1884 a French squadron under Admiral Amédée Courbet sailed up the Min River and anchored near the Fuzhou Navy Yard at Mawei, next to the Chinese Fujian Fleet.

The Qing commanders, ordered not to fire first, did little to prepare. On 23 August 1884 the French opened fire. In under an hour the Fujian Fleet, made up of smaller wooden ships, was destroyed; about 800 Chinese sailors were killed. The French then shelled the navy yard. War was declared days later. Chinese forces later won at Zhennan Pass, but in 1885 China recognized French control of Vietnam.
story_zh: 19世纪80年代初，法国加紧控制清朝的藩属国越南，中法两军在越南北部交战。1884年7月，法国海军将领孤拔率舰队驶入闽江，停泊在马尾的福州船政局附近，紧挨着福建水师。
清朝将领奉命"不准先行开炮"，几乎没有做任何准备。1884年8月23日，法舰突然开火，不到一小时，以小型木壳船为主的福建水师全军覆没，约八百名官兵阵亡。法舰随后炮轰船政局。几天后清朝正式宣战。此后清军虽在镇南关取胜，但1885年中国还是承认了法国对越南的控制。
battle-fuzhou.why: The battle wiped out one of China's new modern fleets in minutes and showed how far Qing naval power still lagged.
battle-fuzhou.why_zh: 这一战在片刻之间就摧毁了中国刚刚建立的一支近代舰队，暴露了清朝海军的落后。

people.name: Zhang Peilun
people.role: Qing official in charge at Fuzhou
people.role_zh: 会办福建海疆事宜的清朝大臣

story: In 1894 a rebellion in Korea drew in troops from both China and Japan, which had modernized fast since 1868. Japan soon attacked, sinking a British ship carrying Chinese soldiers and defeating the Qing army at Pyongyang.

On 17 September 1894 the Beiyang Fleet under Ding Ruchang met the Japanese fleet near the mouth of the Yalu River. In five hours of fighting the Chinese lost five ships; Captain Deng Shichang went down with the Zhiyuan. The fleet retreated to Weihaiwei, where it was trapped and surrendered in February 1895, and Ding killed himself. In the Treaty of Shimonoseki China recognized Korea's independence, gave Japan Taiwan and Penghu and paid 200 million taels.
story_zh: 1894年朝鲜发生农民起义，中日两国都出兵朝鲜。1868年以来迅速走上近代化道路的日本很快挑起战争，击沉运送清军的英国商船，又在平壤击败清军。
1894年9月17日，丁汝昌率领的北洋舰队在鸭绿江口附近与日本舰队交战。激战五小时，北洋舰队损失五艘军舰，致远舰管带邓世昌与舰同沉。舰队退守威海卫，被日军围困，1895年2月投降，丁汝昌自杀。根据《马关条约》，中国承认朝鲜独立，把台湾、澎湖割让给日本，并赔款二亿两白银。
yalu.why: Defeat by a smaller Asian neighbor shocked China, set off a scramble for concessions by the powers and pushed many toward reform or revolution.
yalu.why_zh: 败给一个较小的亚洲邻国震动了全中国，引发列强瓜分狂潮，也促使许多人转向变法或革命。

people.name: Li Hongzhang
people.role: Qing statesman who signed the treaty

story: After the defeat by Japan, the scholar Kang Youwei and his student Liang Qichao called for deep reform on the model of Meiji Japan. The young Guangxu Emperor, eager to act, called Kang to an audience.

From 11 June 1898 the emperor issued a flood of edicts: modern schools and a university in Beijing, an end to the eight-legged essay in the exams, a modern army, new offices for trade and industry, and the closing of useless posts. Officials resisted. On 21 September Empress Dowager Cixi, backed by army leaders, took back power and put Guangxu under house arrest. Kang and Liang fled to Japan, and six reformers, including Tan Sitong, were executed.
story_zh: 甲午战败后，学者康有为和他的学生梁启超呼吁仿效日本明治维新，进行彻底改革。年轻的光绪帝急于有所作为，召见了康有为。
从1898年6月11日起，光绪帝接连颁布诏书：兴办新式学堂，在北京设立京师大学堂，科举废除八股文，编练新军，设立管理工商的新机构，裁撤闲散衙门。官员们百般抵制。9月21日，慈禧太后在军方支持下重新掌权，把光绪帝软禁起来。康有为、梁启超逃往日本，谭嗣同等六人被杀，史称"戊戌六君子"。
hundred-days.why: The failure showed that reform from the top was blocked, and pushed many young Chinese toward revolution.
hundred-days.why_zh: 变法的失败说明自上而下的改革已经走不通，许多年轻人从此转向革命。

quote.zh: 我自横刀向天笑，去留肝胆两昆仑。
quote.en: I laugh to the sky, my sword across me; those who go and those who stay are both as steadfast as the Kunlun mountains.
quote.from: Tan Sitong, written on his prison wall 谭嗣同《狱中题壁》

story: In the late 1890s, in drought-hit Shandong, groups of young men practiced martial arts and rituals they believed made them immune to bullets. Called Boxers by foreigners, they blamed Christian missionaries and converts for the country's troubles, and their slogan was 'Support the Qing, destroy the foreign'.

In 1900 the Boxers spread to Beijing and Tianjin, killing missionaries and Chinese Christians and tearing up railways. In June the German minister was killed, and Cixi declared war on the foreign powers. Boxers and Qing troops besieged the foreign legations for 55 days. In August an army from eight nations fought its way from Tianjin and took Beijing. Cixi and the emperor fled to Xi'an, and foreign troops looted the city.
story_zh: 19世纪90年代末，山东旱灾频发，一些青年练习拳术和仪式，相信自己能刀枪不入，外国人称之为"拳民"。他们把国家的苦难归咎于传教士和教民，口号是"扶清灭洋"。
1900年，义和团涌入北京、天津，杀害传教士和中国教民，拆毁铁路。6月，德国公使被杀，慈禧太后向各国宣战。义和团和清军围攻东交民巷使馆区达五十五天。8月，八国联军从天津一路打进北京。慈禧和光绪帝逃往西安，联军在北京大肆抢掠。
boxers.why: The disaster ended in the Boxer Protocol's crushing indemnity and convinced even the Qing court that it had to reform.
boxers.why_zh: 这场灾难以《辛丑条约》的巨额赔款告终，连清廷也认识到不改革不行了。

story: After the Eight-Nation Alliance occupied Beijing in 1900, the court, which had fled to Xi'an, sent the elderly statesman Li Hongzhang and Prince Qing to negotiate with eleven foreign powers.

The protocol was signed on 7 September 1901. China had to pay an indemnity of 450 million taels of silver, about one tael for each person in China, over 39 years with interest. Officials who had backed the Boxers were executed or exiled, and examinations were suspended in places where foreigners had been killed. The legation quarter in Beijing became a fortified foreign zone, foreign troops were stationed along the railway to the sea, and the Dagu forts were destroyed. Li Hongzhang died two months later.
story_zh: 1900年八国联军占领北京后，逃到西安的清廷派年迈的李鸿章和庆亲王奕劻与十一个国家谈判。
条约于1901年9月7日签订。中国须赔款白银四亿五千万两，相当于每个中国人一两，分三十九年还清，并计利息。支持义和团的官员被处死或流放，外国人被杀的地方停止科举考试。北京东交民巷使馆区成为由外国军队把守的特区，从北京到海口的铁路沿线驻扎外国军队，大沽炮台被拆毁。两个月后，李鸿章去世。
boxer-protocol.why: The protocol crippled Qing finances and marked the low point of Chinese sovereignty. Some of the indemnity was later returned to fund education, including Tsinghua University.
boxer-protocol.why_zh: 《辛丑条约》使清朝财政濒临崩溃，标志着中国主权跌到了谷底。部分赔款后来被退还，用于兴办教育，清华大学就由此而来。

story: For about 1,300 years, since the Sui dynasty, the imperial examinations had been the main road to government office. Candidates spent years memorizing the Confucian classics and writing set-form essays. After 1895 many reformers argued that the system could not produce people who understood science, law or foreign affairs.

The exams had already been changed in 1901, dropping the eight-legged essay. In 1905 the powerful officials Yuan Shikai and Zhang Zhidong asked the court to end them altogether so that new-style schools, which few would attend while the exams still promised office, could grow. An edict in September 1905 abolished the exams. Thousands of young men turned to new schools or went to study abroad, especially in Japan.
story_zh: 从隋朝算起，科举考试作为做官的主要途径已经延续了约一千三百年。考生要花多年时间背诵儒家经典，练习格式固定的文章。1895年以后，许多改革者认为这种制度培养不出懂科学、法律和外交的人才。
1901年科举已经改革，废除了八股文。1905年，重臣袁世凯、张之洞奏请彻底停止科举，因为只要科举还是做官的捷径，新式学堂就很难办起来。同年9月，朝廷下诏废除科举。成千上万的年轻人转入新式学堂，或者出国留学，其中去日本的最多。
exam-abolished.why: Ending the exams broke the link between Confucian learning and power that had shaped Chinese society, and created a new class of students, many of whom became revolutionaries.
exam-abolished.why_zh: 废除科举切断了儒学与权力之间延续千年的纽带，造就了新的知识群体，其中许多人后来走上了革命道路。

story: After 1900 thousands of young Chinese went to study in Japan, and Tokyo became a center of revolutionary ideas. Sun Yat-sen, a doctor from Guangdong, had founded the Revive China Society in 1894 and led failed uprisings. Other groups had formed in Hunan and Zhejiang.

In August 1905 Sun joined with Huang Xing, Song Jiaoren and others in Tokyo to found the Tongmenghui, the 'Revolutionary Alliance', with Sun as leader. Members swore to expel the Manchus, restore China, establish a republic and equalize land rights. The alliance published the newspaper Minbao, raised money among overseas Chinese and launched a series of uprisings in south China. Most failed, but they spread the movement inside the New Army.
story_zh: 1900年以后，成千上万的中国青年到日本留学，东京成了革命思想的中心。广东籍医生孙中山1894年创立兴中会，多次发动起义均告失败。湖南、浙江等地也先后成立了其他革命团体。
1905年8月，孙中山与黄兴、宋教仁等人在东京成立中国同盟会，孙中山任总理。会员宣誓"驱除鞑虏，恢复中华，创立民国，平均地权"。同盟会创办《民报》，在海外华人中募捐，并在华南接连发动起义。这些起义大多失败，但革命思想由此在新军中传播开来。
tongmenghui.why: The Tongmenghui united the revolutionaries and gave them a program. Its members led the 1911 Revolution and later formed the Kuomintang.
tongmenghui.why_zh: 同盟会把各路革命者团结在一起，并提出了明确的纲领。它的成员领导了辛亥革命，后来组成了国民党。

quote.zh: 驱除鞑虏，恢复中华，创立民国，平均地权。
quote.en: Expel the Manchus, restore China, establish a republic, and equalize land rights.
quote.from: Tongmenghui oath, 1905 中国同盟会誓词

story: By 1911 many soldiers in the Qing's modern New Army in Hubei secretly belonged to revolutionary groups. On 9 October a bomb went off by accident in a revolutionary workshop in the Russian concession in Hankou. Police found lists of members, and arrests and executions began.

Facing discovery, soldiers of an engineering battalion in Wuchang rose on the evening of 10 October. The Qing governor-general fled, and by the next morning the rebels held the city. They made Li Yuanhong, a reluctant brigade commander, their military governor and declared a new government. Over the next two months province after province declared independence. Delegates elected Sun Yat-sen provisional president, and the Republic of China was founded on 1 January 1912.
story_zh: 到1911年，湖北新军中已有许多士兵秘密加入革命团体。10月9日，革命党人在汉口俄租界的据点里意外发生炸弹爆炸，警察搜出了成员名册，开始大肆搜捕和处决。
眼看就要暴露，驻武昌的工程营士兵于10月10日晚率先起义。湖广总督逃走，到第二天早上起义军已控制武昌城。他们推举并不情愿的协统黎元洪为都督，宣布成立新政府。此后两个月内，各省纷纷宣布独立。各省代表选举孙中山为临时大总统，1912年1月1日中华民国成立。
wuchang.why: The uprising began the Xinhai Revolution, which ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule. 10 October is still celebrated as the 'Double Tenth'.
wuchang.why_zh: 武昌起义拉开了辛亥革命的序幕，结束了两千多年的帝制。10月10日至今仍作为"双十节"被纪念。

story: In the 1900s Chinese provinces raised money from local gentry, merchants and even farmers to build their own railways. In Sichuan, millions of people held shares in the planned Sichuan–Hankou line. In May 1911 the Qing cabinet announced that the main trunk lines would be nationalized and built with loans from a group of foreign banks.

Shareholders in Sichuan, Hubei, Hunan and Guangdong were furious, especially as Sichuan investors would not get all their money back. In Sichuan a Railway Protection League led strikes and tax boycotts. On 7 September the governor-general, Zhao Erfeng, arrested the league's leaders and his troops fired on the crowds outside his office, killing dozens. Rebellion spread across the province, and the court sent troops from Hubei to restore order.
story_zh: 20世纪初，各省向士绅、商人乃至农民集资，自办铁路。四川有数百万人入股准备修建的川汉铁路。1911年5月，清朝内阁宣布把干线铁路收归国有，并向外国银行团借款修建。
四川、湖北、湖南、广东的股东群情激愤，四川股民的钱更是难以全部收回。四川成立保路同志会，组织罢市、抗粮抗捐。9月7日，四川总督赵尔丰诱捕保路运动领袖，卫兵又向督署外请愿的民众开枪，打死数十人，史称成都血案。四川各地随即爆发起义，清廷急调湖北新军入川镇压。
railway-protection.why: Moving troops out of Hubei weakened the garrison at Wuchang, where the revolution broke out on 10 October.
railway-protection.why_zh: 湖北新军被调走，削弱了武昌的防务，10月10日革命就在武昌爆发了。

people.name: Pu Dianjun
people.role: Leader of the Railway Protection League

story: After the Wuchang Uprising the Qing court recalled Yuan Shikai, the strongest general in the north, as prime minister. Yuan fought the revolutionaries just enough to show his power, then negotiated with them. They agreed that if he arranged the emperor's abdication, he would become president of the new republic.

On 12 February 1912 the Empress Dowager Longyu issued the abdication edict on behalf of the six-year-old Puyi. It handed sovereignty to the whole nation and set up a constitutional republic. In return, the Articles of Favorable Treatment let Puyi keep his title, live in the inner part of the Forbidden City and receive a yearly allowance. Sun Yat-sen resigned, and Yuan became provisional president in March.
story_zh: 武昌起义后，清廷起用北方最有实力的将领袁世凯为内阁总理大臣。袁世凯与革命军打了几仗，显示了实力，随后与对方谈判。双方约定：只要袁世凯促成清帝退位，就由他出任民国大总统。
1912年2月12日，隆裕太后代表六岁的溥仪颁布退位诏书，把统治权交给全国，确定共和立宪国体。作为交换，《清室优待条件》规定溥仪保留皇帝尊号，暂居紫禁城内廷，每年领取优待费。孙中山随即辞职，3月袁世凯就任临时大总统。
abdication.why: The abdication ended the Qing and the imperial system peacefully, but power passed to Yuan Shikai, and China soon fell into division.
abdication.why_zh: 清帝退位以和平方式结束了清朝和帝制，但权力落入袁世凯手中，中国不久便陷入分裂。

people.name: Yuan Shikai
people.role_zh: 内阁总理大臣，后任大总统

quote.zh: 将统治权公诸全国，定为共和立宪国体。
quote.en: We hand over sovereignty to the whole nation and establish a constitutional republic.
